text:
Maya: Noticing strange billing blips in the last hour correlated with streaming resume events. Routes that had failovers show a short window where sessions are double-counted. Console shows ~600 active_sessions, billing pipeline shows ~900 for the same route for ~3m.

Ravi: Which route/region? Any recent rollout that touched resume logic or sticky routing?

Maya: us-central, traffic spiked after the region drain earlier. We rolled a small sticky-routing tweak last night but that was at midnight. This looks like a mid-flight route-swap during resume.

Em: Could be resume-token namespace collision when the session is migrated between shards. If the resume token is reissued while the old connection hasn't fully tombstoned, both sides count active.

Kai: Do we have logs showing resume accept vs old session closure? Sample from proxy:
[2026-04-01T14:02:13Z] resume_request token=tok-xyz route=us-central shard=sh-12
[2026-04-01T14:02:13Z] resume_accepted session_id=sess-888 -> sess-889
[2026-04-01T14:02:14Z] old_session_closed session_id=sess-888 reason=peer_reset
Note the accepted event precedes closure by ~1s. That could be due to async route-handoff.

Ravi: That ordering would cause metrics to briefly record two active sessions. But our counters should be idempotent based on token. What metric key are we using? session_id or resume_token?

Maya: Console uses session_id dedupe, billing uses resume_token dedupe (older pipeline). When the resume creates a new session_id before the old one decrements, the two systems disagree.

Em: Two independent dedupe keys -> race. We need a unified canonical identity for counting, ideally resume_token when present, fallback to session_id if token missing. But changing billing pipeline is risky.

Kai: Telemetry ingestion lag compounds this: console aggregates in near-real-time (~10s), billing pipeline ingests with ~45s latency. If the resume ordering flips between pipelines, the transient difference appears longer.

metrics-bot: Alert: us-central resume_dup_rate > 0.8% for 5m. Threshold 0.5%.

Maya: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) Add a tiny adaptive grace TTL on the console side where session_id counts remain suppressed for (p50_handoff + 500ms). 2) Emit a `resume_in_progress` event on the event bus that both console and billing can shadow-subscribe to for alignment.

Ravi: Adaptive TTL makes sense. Implement per-route p50 sampling and fallback to global default. Also: try a sync-close attempt before accepting resume, with a short 300-500ms deadline behind a feature flag.

Em: Shadow dedupe in billing: compute resume_token-canonical counts but don't affect billing for 7 days. Generate daily deltas per customer for finance review.

Kai: For canary plan: internal traffic 1% -> 5% -> 10% with `sync-close` flag, monitor `resume.sync_close_duration_ms` and `resume.sync_close_failed`. If tail latency for reconnects increases > 10% abort.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1401 opened for us-central resume duplication spike.

Maya: I'll own console aggregator change + banner UX that explains transient inflation and links to diagnostics. Will add unit tests simulating out-of-order events.

Ravi: I'll own proxy change: sampled resume_token emit + sync-close feature flag. Will post PR and canary IDs.

Em: I'll run the billing shadow job and prepare the CSV delta for finance.

Kai: I'll create a Kibana saved search `ResumeHandoffLatency` and a dashboard panel `resume-token-map` sampling 5% of events.

Maya: Thanks all. If anyone sees billing delta > 5% in the canary cohort, pause rollout and notify finance and oncall.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: edge-proxy/feat/resume-sync-close @ 2026-04-01T18:00:00Z (internal canary 1%).

Maya: PRs incoming: console aggregator + banner. Will link once ready.
